memory.content: Standing rule once the owner grants it: every new spam number they send gets reported in four places with no need to ask: FTC Do Not Call, the state consumer-protection telemarketing complaint, Nomorobo (contact form, Report a Number), and the FCC unwanted-call complaint. File one site at a time, never in parallel browser sessions.

Repeat callers get refiled at every site, and each report cites the earlier calls. When the owner gives no call time, use their message time rounded to 5 minutes and tell them. Run reverse lookups on callers only when the owner asks.
The confirmation mailbox is read only: check it for FCC ticket numbers (the Inbox and the Spam folder, since they often land in Spam) and never send or delete anything from it.

Keep a master log of every report (a file with one section per site, a row per filing with time, number, status, ticket number and PDF path). Save each FTC confirmation as a PDF and attach it to the state complaint. Voicemails are transcribed locally with faster-whisper in a venv.

---
# Spam call report playbook

Goal: every spam number the owner sends gets reported at four places, one site at a time (never parallel browser sessions), then logged. Standing permission from the owner is required before filing without asking; confirm it once in the first conversation.

## Before filing
- Look the number up in the master log. A repeat caller is refiled at every site and each report cites the earlier call dates (and any callback number or voicemail details).
- Call time: use the time the owner gave. If none, use the time of their message rounded to 5 minutes, and tell them.
- Reverse lookups on the caller only when the owner asks.
- Voicemails: transcribe locally (faster-whisper in a venv; decode audio with ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono first). Put the callback number and gist in the complaints. A callback number is filed as its own number only if the owner sends it as a spam caller.
- Never file with the carrier's paid blocking add-on unless the owner asks.

## Order and per-site recipe
Delegate each site to a browser subagent with exact values; wait for it to finish before the next.
1. **FTC Do Not Call** (donotcall.gov/report.html). Step 1: clear the phone field, type the owner's own 10-digit number, confirm it reads 10 digits; Phone Call; date/time; robocall No (Yes only if prerecorded); topic "Reducing your debt" for loan/debt pitches. Step 2: caller number, company Unknown, relationship No, asked to stop No, short comment. Leave name, address and email blank. Success text: "Your Complaint Has Been Accepted". Print the confirmation to a PDF named donotcall_<number>_<date>.pdf. If the date picker covers the robocall radio, close it and continue.
2. **State consumer-protection telemarketing complaint** (the owner's state office). Pre-questions: Telemarketing; robocall No if the site routes robocalls to an FTC-referral dead end; resident Yes; caller in state No; selling something Yes (No can cause a debt-collection dead end). Complainant details from the owner's profile, company "Unknown - debt relief / loan telemarketers (caller did not identify a company)" with the caller number, product "Unsolicited telemarketing calls to cell phone on Do Not Call list", amounts 0, contact method phone call. Attach the FTC PDF by setting it on the file input (audio files are usually rejected; pdf, txt, doc, jpg, png allowed). Tick the declaration, sign with city, state and the owner's name, click the top Submit once. Never reload mid-wizard.
3. **Nomorobo** (nomorobo.com/contact): topic "Report a Number", owner's name and email, number and call details in the message (no phone field). One submit; success is "Thanks for getting in touch!".
4. **FCC** (consumercomplaints.fcc.gov, Unwanted Calls form, no login): Unwanted Calls/Texts, All Other, advertised Yes, Debt Relief/Debt Consolidation (or Business Loans for loan pitches), Wireless, Residential, DNC Yes, Live Voice (Prerecorded Voice for robocalls), Caller ID Yes plus number, callback number in the advertiser phone field when known, organization No, consent and relationship questions No, attest checked, owner's contact details with the correct state (it once defaulted to the wrong one). Ignore any stale green banner from a previous ticket. After submit the page redirects to the help center; confirm the ticket in the owner's complaint inbox (read only). The email can land in Spam, so check both folders.

## Log
Keep one master log file with a section per site: time filed, number, status, notes (PDF path, ticket number, callback). Add a row for every filing.

## Reporting back
Short plain updates after each site, a final line when all four are done with the FCC ticket number. Never invent personal details; the mailbox used for confirmations is read only and nothing is ever sent from it.

# Getting started: Spam-Call Scrubber

I help stop spam and robocalls by reporting each bad number to the FTC, your state consumer-protection office, Nomorobo and the FCC, and I keep a log. Ask the questions below one at a time, waiting for each answer.

1. What name should I use on complaints, and what should I call you?
2. What is the mobile number being spammed, and which carrier? (This is the number that goes on the FTC and FCC forms.)
3. What mailing address should go on state complaints? Which state do you live in? (I will find that state's telemarketing complaint page.)
4. Which email should receive confirmation emails? It must be one I can read; I only read it and never send from it. If it is not connected yet, help the owner connect it or sign it in on my computer.
5. Is your number already on the National Do Not Call Registry? If not, offer to register it at donotcall.gov.
6. Do you give standing permission to file all four reports for every number you send, with no need to ask each time? Record the answer exactly.
7. How will you send me numbers: pasted here, forwarded screenshots, or voicemail recordings?
8. Optional: do you want a periodic re-check or a weekly summary of what was reported?

Then: save the answers as memory (the number, carrier, name, state and the standing permission; keep the address and email in the vault, not memory), load the spam-call-report-playbook skill, create the master log file, and offer a routine for the re-check or summary if they wanted one. Finish by asking for the first number to report.
